window: entry run-day close; amc out at next open, bmo out 13:00 ET report day

names.reason: QFIN's 11-24 call disclosed a worsening industry state into Q4: tighter liquidity ahead, Q4 volume down about 20% QoQ, credit not yet turned, and more rules pending. FINV's call must describe the same state with a China book that shrank faster. Its reactions have matched QFIN's sign over four cycles, and in August the sympathy day left a further -15%. But the sell-side cut FINV's FY EPS 36% in a month and already models revenue below the guide's low end, and today's -4.4% on heavy volume took part of the read-through. So the edge is a lean, not a 65% call.
names.what_would_flip_it: The FY revenue guide reaffirmed at RMB11.5bn or more (above the 11.31bn consensus), with Q3 profit well above the roughly RMB200m-a-quarter that consensus implies for H2, and/or a new or enlarged buyback sized against the sub-cash market cap.
names.unpriced: Possibly the second leg of the read-through. FINV took only about 45% of QFIN's move today, but its China volume fell harder than QFIN's in Q3, and its call will have to repeat QFIN's outlook: tighter liquidity, rising credit and collection costs, pending rules, no 2027 visibility. In August the same sympathy-then-own-print pattern left a further -15%. The bias is the market treating the peer read-through as fully absorbed on the peer's day. Partly offset by fresh consensus cuts that already sit below the guide's low end.

names.reason: The sector news since FINV last spoke is negative: Qfin's Q4 guide cut, its 'liquidity squeeze' and its credit erosion. But FINV fell 4.4% today in sympathy and 17.6% over 20 days, and it trades below its cash. Its revenue guide has an overseas cushion that makes a hold at the low end plausible. I cannot show a gap between what the price holds and what the release will reveal, so I make no call.
names.what_would_flip_it: Either of two things would make this a clear short: a formal cut of the FY26 revenue guide below RMB11.5bn, or a Q4 profit outlook like Qfin's together with a paused buyback. Either of two would make it a long: a reaffirmed guide with the buyback continuing, or a new or enlarged buyback or special dividend.

names.reason: The stock trades on a US$6.03 controller take-private bid, which caps the upside and compresses any earnings reaction. QFIN's 11-24 print and today's 4-10% peer sell-off point to a weak sector Q3, which tilts the open downside slightly, but the link from results to deal confidence is weak and the expected move sits inside the deadband on a thin half-day session. The direction lean falls short of the 65 bar.
names.what_would_flip_it: The release carrying deal news: a definitive merger agreement or a committee advisor and process update (up toward 6.03), or a revised or withdrawn proposal (sharply down).
names.unpriced: Possibly the read-through from QFIN's 11-24 print and today's sector sell-off: XYF's price did not move today, because the take-private bid anchors it. But the anchor is the reason the print matters little either way, so the gap is small and asymmetric (capped upside, open downside) rather than a clear mispricing.

names.reason: The price is anchored to a $6.03 controlling-holder offer with a 15% spread, so the Q3 numbers move it only through deal-probability channels that nothing public points to. There is no consensus, no option market and no guide to beat. Peer weakness is visible and already sits in the wide spread. No mechanism clears the 65% bar.
names.what_would_flip_it: The release or call announcing a buyer price cut or withdrawal, or an unexpected financing problem (down hard). Or the special committee naming advisers and starting negotiations alongside a clean credit print (a modest move toward the offer).

names.reason: The evidence that the quarter misses the Bloomberg consensus is dated and fairly strong: BCRA system Q3 ROA 0.8% vs 2.5%, Supervielle's halved profit and 430bp NIM drop, Citi and Goldman 14-19% below consensus, and country risk up about 200bp inside the quarter. But the previews quantifying a miss were public on 11-13, the stock is at the lows near 0.6x book, and the window's open also carries a full Buenos Aires session and the global tape. So the probability that the direction is right does not reach 65.
names.what_would_flip_it: Net income at or above roughly ARS 200bn with NIM holding near 17% (Macro's bond and dollar book carrying the quarter), which would confirm the market's 'insulated quality' view and likely produce a relief open like 3Q25 and 1Q26.
names.unpriced: The Bloomberg consensus (219.5bn) is stale relative to the Q3 system data. The BCRA September report (system Q3 ROA 0.8% vs 2.5% in Q2) came after the 11-13 previews, and Macro's relative strength against peers suggests the market still treats it as insulated. It probably is not fully insulated, but that is only a partial gap: the sell-side previews already quantified a miss.

names.reason: I found no dated evidence of an earnings gap that the price misses and that this release would reveal inside the window. The peers' margin squeeze and provision relief are public, and the previews already carry them. The window also includes a full Argentine session on 11-26 under a live country-risk sell-off, and that session will dominate the 11-27 open.
names.what_would_flip_it: A clear beat with the ~12% adjusted ROE guide held or raised, together with a calm 11-26 local session (Treasury rollover cleared, country risk easing), would argue long. A guide cut like Supervielle's would argue short.
